page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Talking sense
title: Talking sense
topic: Language to use for clearing up confusion
description:
With Paul still out of action following his biscuit-related accident Anna is taking charge at Tip Top Trading. What will she do when she and Tom discover a mysterious note in Paul's office – and how will she stop rumours flying round the office?
This episode focuses on the language that you might use when rumours are spreading and you need to put a stop to them.
phrases: There are some rumours going around that are not true.
I am trying to establish the facts and if I get any information I will let you know straight away.
Ignore the rumours and please don't pass them on.
Please just carry on with your work as normal. Thank you.

listening_challenge.question: What award has Tip Top Trading been nominated for?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to English at Work. Anna is acting up as boss because Paul had an accident with a biscuit! But her and Tom are in a panic after finding a note in Paul's diary that said 'Socrates, IPC, final'. Could it mean bad news for Tip Top Trading? Let’s find out.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It's very odd and it can't be good. But Socrates must mean Mr Socrates.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes – but IPC? What's that mean?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah and final sounds very… final.  Hmm… I've got it! IPC – it must be code for imminent post closures – they're going to sack us all!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sshh. Keep your voice down. Don't tell everyone. Let's check things out first, don't say anything yet. OK?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: OK. Mum's the word.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Your mum knows?!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No, no, no, it's our little secret. See you later.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Everything OK Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh yeah, everything's cool. Actually Denise, it's not. I think we're all going to be sacked tomorrow by Mr Socrates.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: What?! No! I've got a hairdresser's appointment on Saturday, how am I going to pay for it now? What am I going to do? I know, I'll call Marge.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hey Brian, Pete… we're all going to be sacked tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Erm… Anna, you've got a problem brewing.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Tom's spreading rumours about job cuts. Everyone's starting to panic.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh no! I'd better do something but what shall I say?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Call a meeting quickly. Tell the team 'there are some rumours going around that are not true'. Say, 'I am trying to establish the facts and I will let you know as soon as I have some information'. You could say 'I would be grateful if you hear any rumours, not to pass them on'. This can be a tricky situation and you need to handle it well. Good luck!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Gosh. This is hard but here goes. Excuse me, could everyone gather round please.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Is this about the sackings?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No Denise. Any rumours about sackings are not true.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah that's right. Who told you that Denise?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hmmm…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Please don't listen to rumours. I am trying to establish the facts and if I get any information I will let you know straight away.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: But I heard Mr Socrates is coming tomorrow, surely he’s going to sack us.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Ignore the rumours and please don't pass them on.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna. Tell them to carry on with their work as normal.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right, yes. Could you please just carry on with your work as normal. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: So Anna, how are you going to find out the facts?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm going to have to call Paul – in private Tom – I don't want any more rumours getting out.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh yeah, absolutely. You need to establish the facts right?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hello, Paul speaking.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh hi Paul. It's Anna. Sorry to bother you. Are you feeling better?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Much better thanks but keeping clear of biscuits for a while! Anyway, is everything OK?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Not exactly. There are rumours spreading about job cuts. Tom saw a note in your diary for tomorrow that said 'Socrates, IPC'.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hmm. Really? Oh yes. I mean, oh no! It's not job cuts – it's IPC - the International Plastics Conference tomorrow! And Mr Socrates is flying in for it. Oh golly gosh, I'd forgotten about that.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I see. And why did you right final?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Because there's an award being given for the Best Plastic Innovation – and we're in the final with our Imperial Lemon.  It was a reminder to me to write an acceptance speech. Oh golly gosh, I haven't written a thing.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh dear. What are we going to do?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: What are you going to do indeed? But thank goodness those rumours of job cuts are not true. Tomorrow could actually be a good day for Tip Top Trading. Here's a reminder of the phrases Anna used to try and control the spread of some office rumours:
There are some rumours going around that are not true.
Please don't listen to rumours.
I am trying to establish the facts and if I get any information I will let you know straight away.
Ignore the rumours and please don’t pass them on.
Please just carry on with your work as normal. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Tomorrow is going to be an important day at the International Plastics Conference. Mr Socrates will be there and Tip Top Trading could pick up a prestigious prize but who’s going to write the acceptance speech?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: OK Anna, this calls for some urgent action. I want you and Tom to meet me at the Princess Diana Conference Centre tomorrow at 9.00.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right. And what about the speech?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well, I've got quite a lot on my plate so I was wondering if you could give it a go… please?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Me?! I've never done it before. What am I going to say?!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Don't worry Anna. We’re here to help. Join us again soon for some more English at Work. Bye!
